title: Read the arc before forcing the click
summary: Popcorn-style dynamic clicking improves when the player reads the target arc and places ahead of it instead of rushing each click like a panic static flick.
why: Popcorn exposes whether the player can identify the next part of the arc instead of reacting late to where the target just was.
Better reads reduce both panic clicks and excessive lead distance.
actions: Track the whole arc for a moment before committing instead of flicking only to the current target location.
Place slightly ahead of the arc, then reduce how much you lead as timing improves.
If you keep getting surprised by side bounces, slow the click rate until the read is cleaner.
avoid: Do not treat popcorn like a pure static clicking benchmark.
Avoid panic clicking just because the target changed height or direction.

evidence.claim: Popcorn-style tasks emphasize reaction and arc reading rather than simple static-style flicking.
